extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in geometric analysis / geometric topology working on Ricci flow and 3-manifolds
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and assumptions for performing Ricci flow with surgery on three-dimensional compact orientable manifolds: pinching and canonical-neighborhood conditions, derivative and curvature estimates, identification of fine necks/caps for surgery, and the formal definition of a surgically modified solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pinching assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: The eigenvalues λ ≥ µ ≥ ν of the curvature operator at each point and each time satisfy an explicit pinching inequality (7.3.3) whenever ν < 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This quantitative pinching relation is required to hold for the surgically modified solution at every point and time (with the stated accuracy ε). It is an a priori assumption used to control the negative part of curvature during the flow and surgeries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy ε)
rubrics_metrics.description: For given ε > 0 there exist positive constants C1,C2 and a nonincreasing positive function r(t) such that at each time t>0 every point x with scalar curvature R(x,t) ≥ r(t)^{-2} has a neighborhood B (with B_t(x,σ) ⊂ B ⊂ B_t(x,2σ) for some 0<σ<C1 R(x,t)^{-1/2}) which is one of: (a) a strong ε-neck; (b) an ε-cap; or (c) a compact manifold (without boundary) of positive sectional curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further requirements: the scalar curvature in B at time t lies between C1^{-2} R(x,t) and C2 R(x,t); the neighborhood satisfies the gradient estimates (7.3.4); and in cases (a) and (b) the volume satisfies Vol_t(B) ≤ ε σ^3. 'Strong ε-neck' is defined by closeness (after scaling by R(x,t) and time shift) in the C^{[ε^{-1}]} topology to the evolving standard round cylinder on a prescribed space–time subset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gradient / derivative estimates for high-curvature regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform derivative estimates of the form |∂R/∂t| < η R^2 and |∇R| < η R^{3/2} (equations (7.3.1) and (7.3.4)) hold at points with sufficiently large scalar curvature (≥ r0^{-2}), with η a universal constant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These estimates guarantee control of the evolution and spatial variation of scalar curvature near high-curvature points and are used to deduce openness of the bounded-curvature set and to get local compactness / limit arguments. They are part of the condition used to choose r0 so that canonical neighborhoods exist for R ≥ r0^{-2}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of ε-neck, ε-cap, ε-tube, ε-horn, capped ε-horn, double ε-horn
rubrics_metrics.description: An ε-neck (radius r) is an open set which, after scaling by r^{-2}, is ε-close in C^{[ε^{-1}]} topology to S^2 × I with S^2 of scalar curvature 1 and I of length 2ε^{-1}; an ε-cap is a metric on B^3 or RP^3  ar{B}^3 whose outside is an ε-neck and whose end has curvature tending to infinity; ε-tube/horn/double-horn/capped-horn are global structures built by concatenating necks/caps with specified end-behavior (curvature bounded or blowing up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These geometric classifications are used to recognize canonical neighborhoods and to determine where surgery may be performed (e.g., horns are the places where one can find necks suitable for cutting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform surgeries only at ε-horns using 'fine' necks (avoid surgery in ε-tubes/caps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Surgeries should be performed at necks lying inside ε-horns (not at arbitrary ε-necks in ε-tubes or ε-caps), because one can guarantee finding sufficiently 'fine' necks inside horns and avoid accumulating surgical error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: rough surgeries at only ε-accuracy could accumulate errors across many surgeries and prevent later recognition of high-curvature structure. Restricting surgeries to ε-horns (and using finer necks) controls error accumulation and ensures the process can be continued finitely many times in finite intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of fine δ-necks in ε-horns (Lemma 7.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 0<ε≤1/100 and 0<δ<ε (and T>0), there exists h with 0<h<δρ (depending only on δ and r(T)) such that: if x lies in an ε-horn of (Ω, ḡ) with boundary in Ω_ρ and h(x)=R̄(x)^{-1/2}, then the parabolic neighborhood B_T(x, δ^{-1} h(x)) (over the time interval [T - h(x)^2, T]) is, after scaling by h(x)^{-2}, δ-close in C^{[δ^{-1}]} to the corresponding subset of the evolving standard round cylinder (i.e., is a strong δ-neck).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a uniform scale h (independent of the particular surgical solution) at which one can cut — crucial to ensure enough volume is removed at each surgery and to bound the number of surgeries in finite time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabolic strong-neck closeness criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong ε-neck neighborhood means that, after scaling by the scalar curvature at the center and shifting time to zero, the solution on a specified parabolic region is ε-close (in C^{[ε^{-1}]}) to the subset (S^2 × I, evolving round cylinder) on a corresponding parabolic region with scalar curvature 1 at time zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The parabolic (space-time) closeness is required (not merely a spatial slice) to ensure the neck behaves like a cylindrical solution under the Ricci flow for the time-interval necessary to perform surgery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a solution to Ricci flow with surgery
rubrics_metrics.description: A surgically modified solution is a (finite or countably infinite) collection of smooth solutions g_k(t) defined on compact orientable (possibly disconnected) manifolds M_k over time intervals [t_k^-, t_k^+), with limit metrics (Ω_k, ḡ_k) as t → t_k^+, such that for each k the incoming and outgoing limit pieces contain compact (possibly disconnected) isometric submanifolds; identifying these isometric submanifolds across successive pieces yields a global surgically modified solution on the union of time intervals, and times t_k^+ are called surgery times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalizes how separate smooth pieces before and after a surgery are glued together via isometric compact submanifolds of their limiting metrics; it encodes the topology-change bookkeeping required by surgery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that surgery radius h depend only on δ and time T (uniformity principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The choice of the fine-neck radius h (used to locate cutting spheres) must depend only on δ and r(T) (and not on the particular surgical solution), so that at each surgery one can remove a controlled, uniform amount of volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform dependence prevents an inability to bound the number of surgeries and is essential to prove finiteness of surgeries in any finite time interval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standard capped infinite cylinder as model cap and 'standard solution' existence
rubrics_metrics.description: For constructing caps to glue after cutting, use a rotationally symmetric metric on R^3 with nonnegative sectional curvature, positive scalar curvature, and asymptotic to a round semi-infinite cylinder; the Ricci flow with such initial data (a 'standard capped infinite cylinder') exists on a maximal time interval with bounded curvature on each compact time-subinterval (standard solution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard solutions provide canonical caps to glue in during surgery; curvature estimates for these solutions (Proposition 7.3.3) give quantitative control needed to ensure surgeries preserve the a priori assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume upper bound for canonical neighborhoods of neck/cap types
rubrics_metrics.description: In the canonical neighborhood assumption, for cases (a) strong ε-neck and (b) ε-cap, the volume at time t of B satisfies Vol_t(B) ≤ ε σ^3 (with σ the local radius scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This volume upper bound is included to control noncollapsing and to limit the possible number/size of such neighborhoods; it differs slightly from Perelman's original formulation by adding this explicit volume control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and scaling conventions for identifying canonical neighborhoods
rubrics_metrics.description: When verifying canonical neighborhoods, one scales by the local scalar curvature R(x,t) (or by h(x)^{-2} for fine necks) and shifts time so that the center-time is zero; closeness is measured in C^{[ε^{-1}]} topology on prescribed spatial and parabolic scales (lengths like 2ε^{-1} and time intervals comparable to the squared scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This precise normalization is required to compare local geometry with the standard cylinder/round models and to ensure the neighborhood types are recognized consistently across scales and times.
